is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on the two-spotted spider mite, Tetranychus urticae (Acari: Tetranychidae), an agricultural pest (Title, Abstract, Introduction).

reports_target_markers.evidence: No Anopheles target resistance markers are genotyped; the study focuses on spider mite genes CYP392A16, CYP392E6-8, and CPR.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No target marker genotype data for Anopheles are reported.

african_field_population.evidence: The study investigates laboratory strains and crosses of Tetranychus urticae, not African field Anopheles populations.

is_primary_study.evidence: The article is a primary empirical research study characterizing resistance genetics via bulked segregant analysis in spider mites.

sub_country_location.evidence: No field collection locations for Anopheles are relevant or reported.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: No field mosquito collection timeframes are present.

duplicate_risk.evidence: Not applicable; not an Anopheles study.

supplement.evidence: No relevant mosquito data exists in the main text or supplements.

assessment.summary: This study analyzes the polygenic basis of pyflubumide resistance in the two-spotted spider mite (Tetranychus urticae) using bulked segregant analysis, transcriptomics, and in vitro functional expression of CYP392A16 and CPR.
exclusion_reasons: Studies Tetranychus urticae (spider mites), not Anopheles mosquitoes
Does not genotype target insecticide resistance markers
Does not study African field populations
